old-building-hotel-conversion-approvals-.title: 旧楼改做酒店，新政说“可保持原土地用途”，业主还要过哪几道关？
old-building-hotel-conversion-approvals-.titleEn: Converting an Old Building into a Hotel: The New Policy Says the Original Land Use Can Stay, but What Other Approvals Does the Owner Still Need?
old-building-hotel-conversion-approvals-.description: 三部门意见允许土地权利人在符合规划管控、安全等要求下，用现有房产兴办文化和旅游接待设施时保持原土地用途。本文说明它放宽了什么、酒店是否在内要看地方认定，以及土地、规划建设许可、消防设计审查或备案、营业前消防检查、特种行业许可五关的先后、谁批和停止条件。
old-building-hotel-conversion-approvals-.descriptionEn: The three-ministry Opinions allow a land rights holder, where planning controls, safety and other requirements are met, to keep the original land use when using existing property to set up cultural and tourism visitor reception facilities. This article explains what that relaxation covers, that whether a hotel is included depends on local confirmation, and the order, approving authority and stopping conditions of the five steps: land, planning and construction permits, fire protection design review or filing, the pre-opening fire safety inspection, and the special industry license.
old-building-hotel-conversion-approvals-.author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
content: 旧楼改酒店，新政放宽的是土地这一关：在符合规划管控、安全等要求的前提下，土地权利人用现有房产兴办文化和旅游接待设施，可以保持原土地用途和权利类型不变。规划建设许可、消防设计审查或备案、营业前消防安全检查、特种行业许可这几关，政策没有说可以免，业主仍要按顺序逐关拿到书面结果。
这句话出自自然资源部、文化和旅游部、国家林业和草原局《关于优化自然资源配置 推动旅游业规范有序发展的指导意见》，落款2026年7月23日，文化和旅游部9月15日公开。它确实为持有闲置办公楼、商业楼或厂房的业主减少了一道手续，但“土地用途可以不改”和“这栋楼可以开酒店”是两件事。
## 新政到底放宽了哪一关？

土地用途，是出让合同或划拨文件写明的这块地做什么用，例如商业、办公或工业。按《城市房地产管理法》第十八条，要改变出让合同约定的土地用途，须取得出让方和城市规划主管部门同意，变更或重签出让合同，并相应调整出让金。意见第四条让符合条件的项目可以不走这一步；申请办理用地手续的，经批准可以协议方式办理，也就是不经招标、拍卖、挂牌，由主管部门与现有权利人协商办理。能省多少钱，取决于当地地价和原合同，本文不作估算。
这条放宽有三个前提。第一，规划和安全是条件，不是放宽之后自动得到的结果。第二，主体是“土地权利人”；楼是租来的，由承租人改酒店是否适用，原文没有写。第三，存量工业用地和老旧厂房另有5年过渡期，但要求不改变用地主体和规划条件，只有用地性质可以不同。规划条件，是规划部门给地块定的容积率、建筑高度等指标；要加层、加面积，或换一家公司持有，就用不上这项政策。
意见第五条还写明，严禁借旅游项目之名擅自改变土地现状和规划用途，用于建别墅、私家庄园、房地产等。
过渡期满怎么办，意见没有写。自然资源部办公厅《产业用地政策实施工作指引（2019年版）》第二十条的一般规定是：过渡期以5年为限，过渡期满及涉及转让需办理改变用地主体和规划条件手续的，除符合《划拨用地目录》可保留划拨的以外，可以协议方式办理，但规定或合同约定应收回重新出让的除外。新意见是否照此处理，本文不作推断。测算时可先按5年算一次回本，把第6年起的用地费用单列为未知项。
## 酒店算不算“文化和旅游接待设施”？

意见没有定义这个词，也没有写到酒店。有的地方在楼宇功能转换的文件里已经写明酒店，这不是对“接待设施”的解释，但能说明当地的态度。《上海市人民政府办公厅关于推进商务楼宇更新提升的实施意见》（沪府办发〔2025〕13号）允许地区中心的商务楼宇兼容商业酒店等功能。珠海市自然资源局2026年6月印发的《珠海市既有商业办公建筑功能临时变更为酒店功能使用管理办法（试行）》，把酒店功能界定为以住宿为主的酒店、宾馆、旅馆，变更期限不超过5年。
这两份文件都早于三部门意见，适用的是各自城市。截至2026年11月10日，本文没有查到意见发布后专门落实这一条的地方细则。业主所在城市是否把酒店认作接待设施，应以当地自然资源部门的书面答复为准。
## 旧楼改酒店，土地之后的审批按什么顺序走？
下面按先后列出这五关。每一关写清谁批、什么情况会触发、过不了会卡住哪项投资决定。
第一关，土地。谁批：当地自然资源部门。触发：用现有房产改办酒店，想保持原土地用途。要拿到：能否按原土地用途办理的书面答复。过不了卡住：不能签品牌或管理合同，不能付品牌保证金。
第二关，规划和建设许可。谁批：当地规划、住建部门，各地分工不同。触发：改变建筑使用功能，或改造涉及结构、面积、外立面。要拿到：规划建设手续的书面意见，涉及承重结构变动的，还要有设计单位的设计方案。过不了卡住：不能出施工图，不能定装修总价。
第三关，消防设计审查或备案。谁批：住建部门。触发：按改造后的酒店规模分档，总建筑面积超过一万平方米的做设计审查和消防验收，其余做验收备案。要拿到：审查合格意见，或备案凭证。过不了卡住：特殊建设工程审查不合格不能施工；备案类工程验收备案抽查不合格要停止使用。
第四关，营业前消防安全检查。谁批：当地消防救援机构。触发：酒店属于公众聚集场所，投入使用、营业前必须办理。要拿到：营业前消防安全检查许可。过不了卡住：不能开业，不能在订房平台上线。
第五关，特种行业许可。谁批：县级以上地方公安机关。触发：经营接待旅客住宿的业务。要拿到：特种行业许可证。过不了卡住：不能接待住客。
第一关和第二关可以同时去问，一个问土地，一个问建筑。第二关的结构结论要先于第三关的消防设计，否则消防方案可能落在动不了的墙上。
## 规划和结构这一关，各地怎么管？
北京市规划和自然资源委员会2023年的《北京市建设用地功能混合使用指导意见（试行）》写明，存量建筑用途转换经批准后依法办理规划建设手续。珠海的办法规定，经区政府同意的项目，在不增加建筑面积、高度、层数，不改外立面风格，不影响结构安全的前提下，免于申领建设工程规划许可证，但改造中仍要按建设、消防和行业主管部门的规定办理审批。东莞的正面清单里，改住宿只出现在商业楼和办公楼两栏，厂房一栏没有。
结构安全没有放宽。珠海要求申请人委托有相应资质的设计单位，确认功能变更后符合建筑结构和消防安全规范。《建设工程质量管理条例》第十五条规定，涉及建筑主体和承重结构变动的装修，施工前须由原设计单位或有相应资质的设计单位提出设计方案，没有方案不得施工。
## 为什么要按面积分档看消防？
《建设工程消防设计审查验收管理暂行规定》第十四条把总建筑面积大于一万平方米的宾馆、饭店列为特殊建设工程。这类工程未经消防设计审查或审查不合格不得施工，未经消防验收或验收不合格禁止投入使用。一万平方米以下的，按其他建设工程实行备案抽查，抽查不合格的应当停止使用。
改用途会让分档变化。一栋原本不属于特殊建设工程的办公楼，整栋改成一万平方米以上的酒店，就成了特殊建设工程，开工时间要等审查结果。标准也可能变。广州的既有建筑改造利用办法规定，改变使用功能的，应执行现行国家工程建设消防技术标准，不能按建楼当年的标准。
## 营业前检查和特种行业许可，为什么不是走过场？
《消防法》第七十三条把宾馆、饭店列为公众聚集场所，第十五条规定其营业前消防安全检查实行告知承诺管理。承诺之后有核查。第五十八条规定，核查发现使用、营业情况与承诺不符的，责令停止使用或停产停业，并处三万元以上三十万元以下罚款；限期不改或改后仍不达标的，依法撤销许可。
《旅馆业治安管理办法》第四条规定，开办旅馆应取得营业执照，并向当地公安机关申领特种行业许可证后，方准开业。福建省公安厅2023年的通知实行告知承诺，发证后要把场所书面通报同级市场监管、住建、自然资源、应急救援等部门。前几关留下的缺口，可能在这里暴露。
以下为方法示例，并非真实项目：一位业主有一栋八层旧办公楼，约一万二千平方米，土地是自己的出让地。改成酒店后超过一万平方米，属于特殊建设工程。如果设计单位确认需要大面积加固，或者消防方案要新增疏散楼梯而楼体做不到，就应在设计费和装修款花出去之前暂停，比较只改部分楼层或转作其他用途。
## 什么情况下应该停下来？
出现任何一种，都应回到投资会重新决定：当地不认可按原土地用途办理，改用途的费用让测算不成立；结构加固费用或工期超出可接受范围；消防按现行标准做不到；厂房项目要换持有主体或改规划条件；回本期超过5年，第6年起的用地安排还说不清。
分工要先定。业主或投资决策会定可接受的投入和回本期；项目负责人按顺序组织办理；法务、设计单位分别出书面意见；财务每拿到一关结果就更新测算。推进是否到位，看每关的书面结果是否到手，不看效果图改了几轮。
这套顺序针对城市里的旧办公楼、商业楼和厂房。乡村民宿、住宅楼改造和文物建筑另有专门规定或限制，不宜套用。本文是投资判断的组织方法，不能替代具体项目的法律意见、工程鉴定或审批结论。

contentEn: What the new policy relaxes is the land step. Provided that planning controls, safety and other requirements are met, a land rights holder that uses existing property to set up cultural and tourism visitor reception facilities may keep the original land use and type of land rights unchanged. The policy does not say that the planning and construction permits, the fire protection design review or filing, the pre-opening fire safety inspection or the special industry license can be waived. The owner still has to obtain a written result at each of these steps, in order.

The provision comes from the Guiding Opinions on Optimizing the Allocation of Natural Resources to Promote the Standardized and Orderly Development of Tourism, issued by the Ministry of Natural Resources, the Ministry of Culture and Tourism and the National Forestry and Grassland Administration. The document is dated July 23, 2026, and was made public by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism on September 15. It does remove one procedure for owners of vacant office buildings, commercial buildings or factories. But "the land use need not change" and "this building can open as a hotel" are two different things.
## Which step does the new policy actually relax?

Land use is what the land grant contract or allocation document says the plot is for, such as commercial, office or industrial use. Under Article 18 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, changing the land use agreed in a land grant contract requires the consent of the grantor and the city planning authority, an amended or new grant contract, and a corresponding adjustment to the land grant premium. Article 4 of the Opinions lets qualifying projects skip this step. Where land use procedures are applied for, they may, once approved, be handled by agreement: the authority negotiates directly with the existing rights holder instead of going through tender, auction or listing. How much this saves depends on local land prices and the original contract, and this article does not estimate it.

The relaxation comes with three conditions. First, planning and safety are prerequisites, not results that follow automatically once the rule is relaxed. Second, it applies to the "land rights holder." If the building is leased, the text does not say whether a tenant converting it into a hotel is covered. Third, existing industrial land and old factories get a separate five-year transition period, but the land user and the planning conditions must not change; only the land use category may differ. Planning conditions are the indicators the planning authority sets for a plot, such as floor area ratio and building height. A project that adds floors or floor area, or moves the property into a different company, cannot use this policy.

Article 5 of the Opinions also states that using tourism projects as a pretext to change the current state of land or its planned use without authorization, in order to build villas, private estates or real estate developments, is strictly prohibited.

The Opinions do not say what happens when the transition period ends. The general rule is in Article 20 of the Guidelines for the Implementation of Industrial Land Use Policies (2019 Edition), issued by the General Office of the Ministry of Natural Resources: the transition period is limited to five years. When it expires, or a transfer requires changing the land user and planning conditions, the procedures may be handled by agreement, except where the land qualifies under the Catalogue of Allocated Land to remain allocated, and except where rules or the contract require the land to be taken back and granted again. This article does not infer whether the new Opinions will follow the same approach. For financial modelling, one option is to test payback over five years first and list land costs from year six onward as an unknown.
## Does a hotel count as a "cultural and tourism visitor reception facility"?

The Opinions do not define the term and do not mention hotels. Some local documents on converting building functions already name hotels explicitly. That is not an interpretation of "visitor reception facilities," but it does show the local stance. The Implementation Opinions of the General Office of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government on Promoting the Renewal and Upgrading of Commercial Office Buildings (Hu Fu Ban Fa [2025] No. 13) allow commercial office buildings in district centers to accommodate compatible functions such as commercial hotels. The Zhuhai Measures for the Administration of the Temporary Change of Existing Commercial and Office Buildings to Hotel Use (Trial) (Zhu Zi Ran Zi [2026] No. 234), issued by the Zhuhai Natural Resources Bureau in June 2026, define hotel use as hotels, guesthouses and inns mainly providing accommodation, with a change period of no more than five years.

Both documents predate the three-ministry Opinions and apply only to their own cities. As of November 10, 2026, this article found no local implementing rules issued after the Opinions specifically to carry out this provision. Whether an owner's city treats hotels as visitor reception facilities should be confirmed by a written reply from the local natural resources authority.
## After land, in what order do the approvals for converting an old building into a hotel run?
The five steps are listed below in sequence. Each one sets out who approves it, what triggers it, and which investment decision is blocked if it fails.

Step 1: Land. Who approves: the local natural resources authority. Trigger: converting existing property into a hotel while keeping the original land use. What to obtain: a written reply on whether the project can proceed under the original land use. If it fails, it blocks: signing a brand or management contract and paying a brand deposit.

Step 2: Planning and construction permits. Who approves: the local planning and housing and urban-rural development authorities, with the division of responsibilities varying by locality. Trigger: changing the building's use, or renovation that affects structure, floor area or facade. What to obtain: written opinions on the planning and construction procedures and, where load-bearing structures are altered, a design scheme from a design institute. If it fails, it blocks: producing construction drawings and fixing the total fit-out cost.

Step 3: Fire protection design review or filing. Who approves: the housing and urban-rural development authority. Trigger: tiered by the size of the converted hotel. Projects with a total floor area above 10,000 square meters go through design review and fire protection acceptance; all others go through acceptance filing. What to obtain: a design review approval or a filing certificate. If it fails, it blocks: a special construction project cannot start work if it fails the design review, and a filing project must stop being used if it fails the spot check on its acceptance filing.

Step 4: Pre-opening fire safety inspection. Who approves: the local fire and rescue agency. Trigger: a hotel is a public gathering place and must complete this before it is put into use or opens for business. What to obtain: a pre-opening fire safety inspection permit. If it fails, it blocks: opening, and going live on booking platforms.

Step 5: Special industry license. Who approves: a local public security authority at or above the county level. Trigger: operating a business that accommodates guests. What to obtain: a special industry license. If it fails, it blocks: accepting guests.

Steps 1 and 2 can be raised at the same time, one about the land and one about the building. The structural conclusion from Step 2 must come before the fire protection design in Step 3; otherwise the fire protection plan may rely on walls that cannot be moved.
## How do different localities handle planning and structure?

The Beijing Guiding Opinions on Mixed Use of Construction Land Functions (Trial) (Jing Gui Zi Fa [2023] No. 313), issued in 2023 by the Beijing Municipal Commission of Planning and Natural Resources, state that once a change of use for an existing building is approved, planning and construction procedures must be completed in accordance with the law. Under the Zhuhai measures, projects approved by the district government are exempt from applying for a construction project planning permit, provided they do not increase floor area, height or number of floors, do not change the style of the facade, and do not affect structural safety; the renovation must still go through approvals under the rules of the construction, fire protection and industry authorities. In Dongguan's positive list, conversion to accommodation appears only under commercial and office buildings, not under factories.

Structural safety has not been relaxed. Zhuhai requires applicants to engage a design institute with the appropriate qualifications to confirm that the building will meet structural and fire safety codes after the change of use. Article 15 of the Regulations on the Quality Management of Construction Projects provides that, for renovation involving changes to the main structure or load-bearing structure, the original design institute or a design institute with the appropriate qualifications must produce a design scheme before work starts, and no work may start without one.
## Why look at fire protection by floor area tier?

Article 14 of the Interim Provisions on the Administration of Fire Protection Design Review and Acceptance of Construction Projects lists hotels and guesthouses with a total floor area above 10,000 square meters as special construction projects. Such projects may not start construction without passing the fire protection design review, and may not be put into use without passing the fire protection acceptance inspection. Projects of 10,000 square meters or less are treated as other construction projects subject to filing and spot checks, and must stop being used if they fail the spot check.

A change of use can move a building into a different tier. An office building that was not a special construction project becomes one when the whole building is converted into a hotel of more than 10,000 square meters, and construction then has to wait for the review result. The applicable standards may also change. Guangzhou's measures on renovating and reusing existing buildings require projects that change use to follow current national fire protection technical standards for construction, not the standards in force when the building was built.
## Why are the pre-opening inspection and special industry license more than a formality?

Article 73 of the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China lists hotels and guesthouses as public gathering places, and Article 15 subjects their pre-opening fire safety inspection to the notification-and-commitment system. Commitments are followed by verification. Under Article 58, if verification finds that the actual use or operation does not match the commitment, the venue will be ordered to stop using the premises or suspend operations and fined between RMB 30,000 and RMB 300,000. If it fails to correct the problem within the deadline, or still does not meet the requirements after correction, the permit will be revoked in accordance with the law.

Article 4 of the Measures for the Administration of Public Security in the Hotel Industry provides that a hotel may open only after obtaining a business license and applying to the local public security authority for a special industry license. A 2023 notice from the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department adopted the notification-and-commitment system and requires that, once a license is issued, the premises be reported in writing to the market regulation, housing and urban-rural development, natural resources, emergency management and rescue and other authorities at the same level. Gaps left over from earlier steps may surface here.

The following is an illustrative example, not a real project: an owner has an eight-story old office building of about 12,000 square meters on land granted to the owner. Once converted into a hotel, it exceeds 10,000 square meters and becomes a special construction project. If the design institute confirms that extensive reinforcement is needed, or the fire protection plan calls for a new evacuation staircase that the building cannot accommodate, the owner should pause before spending the design fee and fit-out budget, and compare converting only some floors or switching to another use.
## When should you stop?

If any of the following occurs, the decision should go back to the investment committee: the locality does not accept proceeding under the original land use, and the cost of changing the land use breaks the financial model; the cost or timeline of structural reinforcement exceeds what is acceptable; fire protection cannot meet current standards; a factory project would need a new holding entity or changed planning conditions; or payback takes longer than five years and land arrangements from year six onward remain unclear.

Roles should be settled first. The owner or the investment committee sets the acceptable investment and payback period. The project lead organizes the approvals in sequence. Legal counsel and the design institute each provide written opinions. Finance updates the model each time a step's result comes in. Whether the project is on track should be judged by whether each step's written result is in hand, not by how many rounds of renderings have been revised.

This sequence is designed for old office buildings, commercial buildings and factories in cities. Rural homestays, residential building conversions and heritage buildings are subject to separate rules or restrictions, and this sequence should not be applied to them. This article is a method for organizing investment decisions. It does not replace legal advice, engineering assessment or approval decisions on a specific project.
